title: stochastic-output-oddities-playbook-ivy-gomez
content:
Purpose
-----
Quick personal playbook for triaging weird/stochastic output patterns in hosted/private inference. Meant as a shortcut when I get a Slack ping like: "model started hallucinating dates / repeating phrases / style drift". Keep this lightweight — mostly commands, quick rubrics, sample cases and hypotheses to test.

Notes-to-self style: not polished, partial commands, TODOs scattered.

Top-level checklist (first 10 minutes)
- Reproduce: capture 5-10 raw request->response pairs with exact prompt + headers (model_id, temp, top_p, max_tokens, instructions).
- Check versioning: are requests hitting the same model binary / variant? (model_id + model_version header).
- Check load/noise: any elevated latencies or 5xx rates in the period? (Console traces / route metrics).
- Recent rollouts? Canary/A-B? (Check rollouts dashboard + PRs).
- Compare to baseline: sample from earlier day for same prompt set (if we have saved eval sets).
- Tag severity: "minor (style) / medium (accuracy drop) / major (contradiction/hallucination)".

Ad-hoc rubric for triage (quick scores to surface to PM/SRE)
- Reproducibility (0-3): 0 = one-off, 3 = same on 10/10 runs
- Scope (0-3): 0 = single customer/order, 3 = cross-tenant or public examples
- Magnitude (0-3): 0 = tiny phrasing, 3 = factually wrong consequences (legal/finance)
- Likely cause score (0-3): based on quick checks below (model drift, prompt tempo, infra flakiness)
- Total /9, flag if >=6 for escalation

Quick commands / queries I usually run
- Pull raw requests for user X: db query or audit log -> filters by request_time window + model_id
- Re-run locally with seed list: python eval_runner.py --model X --prompt-file problematic_prompts.txt --n 20 --temp 0.0 0.7 1.0
- Compare tokens: scripts/compare_tokenization.py --orig example.json --current sample.json
- Check KV cache TTLs / warmup behavior in Dedicated: inspect instance metrics around cache_misses

Common hypotheses and how to test them
1) Increased sampling temperature / config drift:
   - Check request attributes (temp, top_p). If client-side changed defaults after SDK update, that'll explain higher variance. Test: re-run exact request with original temp and with observed temp.
2) Model binary change / quantization mismatch:
   - Check model_version header and the last deployment changelog. If new compile flags or q4_0->q4_1 switch happened, re-run with old binary (if still available) to compare.
3) Prompt truncation / instruction truncation due to context window changes:
   - Verify token counts, chunking logic. Recreate prompt with same tokenization and confirm lost instruction tokens.
4) Inference engine nondeterminism (race on KV cache or sharded RNG):
   - Re-run same request multiple times with deterministic flags (seed, disable certain optimizations). If nondet persists only in certain backends, correlate with node_id and kernel versions.
5) Bad prefix caching or cache poisoning:
   - Look for repeated prefixes across bad outputs. Flush cache for route and re-test.
6) Degenerate user prompts / adversarial inputs getting through content filter (rare but possible):
   - Check moderation logs, prefilter behavior.

Sample cases (copied from recent triage for reference)
- Case A: customer asked for a date-anchored summary; model started returning future dates (e.g., 2035). Reproducible 7/10 at temp 0.7, 1/10 at temp 0.0. Hypothesis: sampling + prompt under-specification. Action: enforce temp=0.0 for date tasks or add explicit instruction.
- Case B: short-answer reranking returned empty string for some prompts. Occurred after a low-latency kernel roll. Root cause: tokenization offset mismatch for some BytePair merges -> empty outputs for short inputs. Patch: revert kernel and run targeted regression.
- Case C: style drift (tone became more informal). Not reproducible on deterministic runs; spike correlated with high CPU saturation on a node pool running mixed-precision kernels. Hypothesis: fallback to slower but higher-variance kernels. Action: scope node pool, isolate heavy jobs.

Regression triage notes (how I record evidence)
- Save a small artifact folder: /tmp/oddity-<YYYYMMDD>/{requests.json, responses.json, reruns.json, notes.txt}. Zip and attach to Jira.
- Annotate with exact model_version + infra metadata (region, node id, runtime sha).
- When filing JIRA: include sample before/after and rubric scores. Use JIRA template: Regression > Model > Severity.

Mini experiments to run before escalating
- Deterministic sweep: n=25 runs at temp 0.0, top_p 1.0. If issue disappears, flag sampling config.
- Alternate binary: if q8 vs q4 differences suspected, re-run both and diff outputs.
- Tiny-context stress: reduce prompt to minimal instruction to see if prefix/caching is the issue.
- Replay under load: run synthetic traffic at same RPS to reproduce environmental effects.

When to escalate to eng-on-call / SRE / product
- Escalate immediately if: reproducible major factual errors causing customer harm, or wide cross-tenant impact.
- Otherwise: open JIRA with steps-to-repro, attach artifact and rubric scores. Ping owner on Slack with short summary and link.

Open questions / TODOs
- Can we add a light-weight button in Console to re-run a request deterministically (temp/seed) and show diffs? Low effort, high value.
- Add a small auto-rubric generator in traces that flags >=6.
- Improve audit logs to include model_binary_sha and kernel_version per request (currently sampled, need 100% coverage).

Scratch hypotheses for follow-ups
- H1: A nightly cron that compiles models on a subset of nodes left an inconsistent kernel artifact (check release-engineering).
- H2: New SDK changed client default top_p in v2.3.0 (check PRs).

Small timeline notes (who to ping)
- Release eng: @Mateo (for binary/compile artifacts)
- Serving runtime: #serving-runtime channel (kernel changes)
- SDK: @Priya (client default changes)
- SRE: oncall if infra correlated

Final quick template for Jira description (copy/paste)
- Short summary: one sentence
- Steps to reproduce: exact prompt, flags, model_id/version, timestamps
- Observed behavior: paste 3 examples (raw)
- Expected behavior: short statement
- Quick checks done: reproduce attempts, temp sweep, compare binaries, infra checks
- Artifacts: link to zip + rubric score

Random notes I scribbled during last incident
- Add "deterministic-mode=on" flag to public API? (security + reproducibility tradeoffs)
- Could be useful to log seed when temp>0 for better postmortems

End of playbook. Keep this short and actionable. Update as I learn new patterns.

-- Ivy
   quick list of useful commands in repo: 
   - scripts/regression_collect.sh --start 2026-02-19T22:00 --end 2026-02-19T23:00 --out /tmp/zip
   - python tools/diff_outputs.py /tmp/zip/old.json /tmp/zip/new.json --metrics 'levenshtein,bert_score'
